Example of the new democratic style: Franklin Plummer
column2: Plummer beat a wealthy Natchez rival by posing as champion of the "meritorious poor man," milking a family's cow and picking bugs off a toddler, then lost his followers when he himself bought a stylish coach and a uniformed servant.

column1: Example of the "corrupt bargain"
column2: Jackson had 99 electoral votes to Adams's 84, but Clay, already eliminated with 37, met privately with Adams and rallied the House, and two days after Adams's election Clay was named secretary of state.

column1: Example of mass politics at Jackson's inauguration
column2: About 15,000 supporters thronged the White House, breaking glass, furniture, and mirrors until Jackson fled; Amos Kendall called it a proud day for the people, and Justice Joseph Story said "the reign of King Mob seemed triumphant."

column1: Example of Cherokee accommodation: a written constitution
column2: The Cherokees adopted a U.S.-style constitution, imposed the death penalty for selling land without council consent, and published the bilingual Cherokee Phoenix, a strategy of accommodation led by mixed-bloods under John Ross.

column1: Example of the Trail of Tears
column2: Georgia kidnapped Chief John Ross, a treaty made without him required the Cherokees to leave, and Van Buren's army then forced about 15,000 west, of whom about one-quarter died.

column1: Example of military resistance: Black Hawk and Osceola
column2: Black Hawk's Sauk and Fox recrossed the Mississippi into Illinois and were crushed, while Osceola's Seminoles held out in the Florida Everglades until 1842, the last of the removals.

column1: Example of Jackson ignoring the Court: Worcester v. Georgia
column2: The Marshall Court held that Georgia could not extend its laws over the Cherokees, but Jackson called the decision "stillborn," refused to enforce it, and removal continued.

column1: Example of northern Black disenfranchisement
column2: Black men could vote equally only in five New England states; New York's $250 property requirement, applied only to Black voters, disenfranchised about 90 percent of adult Black males, and New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Connecticut took the vote away.

column1: Example of two views of colonization: Clay and David Walker
column2: Henry Clay told the American Colonization Society that free Blacks were "aliens" who should be sent away to make "one homogeneous people," while David Walker's Appeal called colonization a plot and, quoting Richard Allen, said "this land which we have watered with our tears and our blood is now our mother country."

column1: Example of the Nullification Crisis's climax
column2: A South Carolina convention declared the tariffs of 1828 and 1832 "null, void, and no law," Jackson proclaimed the Union perpetual and signed a Force Bill, and on the same day he also signed a lower tariff, after which South Carolina repealed its ordinance.

column1: Example of Webster's reply to Hayne
column2: When Robert Hayne outlined nullification in the Senate, Daniel Webster answered that "it is the people's constitution, the people's government, made for the people, made by the people, and answerable to the people," and he endorsed judicial review.

column1: Example of Jackson's Bank veto in his own words
column2: Jackson told Van Buren, "The Bank is trying to kill me, but I will kill it," vetoed the early recharter as unconstitutional and a grant of special privilege, and pledged to protect "the humble members of society—the farmer, mechanics, and laborers."

column1: Example of destroying the Bank: removal of the deposits
column2: Jackson changed Treasury secretaries until Roger Taney agreed to shift federal deposits into "pet" state banks; Biddle caused a brief panic, but Jackson refused to restore the deposits, and the charter expired with no national bank to replace it.

column1: Example of the first modern presidential campaign: 1840
column2: Whigs portrayed William Henry Harrison with "log cabins and hard cider," though he lived in a 16-room mansion, painted Van Buren as an aristocrat in corsets and cologne, and won with nearly four-fifths of eligible voters turning out.
